circle: A round, flat shape whose boundary stays the same distance from its center.
Draw a circle around the correct answer.
square: A flat shape with four equal sides and four right angles.
The tile is a square with equal sides.
triangle: A flat shape with three straight sides and three corners.
The sign has the shape of a triangle.
rectangle: A flat shape with four straight sides and four right angles.
Draw a rectangle around the address.
oval: A rounded, flat shape that is longer in one direction.
The mirror has an oval frame.
diamond: A four-sided shape with equal sides, usually shown resting on one corner.
The pattern has a diamond in the center.
pentagon: A flat shape with five straight sides and five corners.
Draw a pentagon with five sides.
hexagon: A flat shape with six straight sides and six corners.
Each cell has the shape of a hexagon.
octagon: A flat shape with eight straight sides and eight corners.
The stop sign is an octagon.
star: A flat shape with points extending outward from its center.
Place a star beside your favorite design.
sphere: A round solid whose surface stays the same distance from its center.
The model globe is a sphere.
cube: A solid shape with six equal square faces.
Each face of the cube is the same size.
cylinder: A solid with two equal, parallel circular ends joined by a curved surface.
The can has the shape of a cylinder.
cone: A solid with a circular base that narrows to one point.
The party hat has the shape of a cone.
pyramid: A solid with a polygon base and triangular faces meeting at one point.
The paper pyramid has a pointed top.
prism: A solid with two matching, parallel polygon bases joined by flat faces.
The glass prism separates the light into colors.
cuboid: A solid shape with six rectangular faces and eight corners.
The shipping box is a cuboid.
hemisphere: One half of a solid ball, divided through its center.
The bowl is shaped like a hemisphere.
torus: A ring-shaped solid or surface with a hole through the middle.
The model torus looks like a doughnut.
tetrahedron: A solid shape with four triangular faces and four corners.
The tetrahedron has four triangular faces.
line: A straight path that extends endlessly in both directions in geometry.
Mark two points on the line.
curve: A line or boundary that bends rather than staying straight.
Follow the curve along the edge of the drawing.
straight: Continuing in one direction without bending or turning.
Use a ruler to draw a straight mark.
zigzag: A path or pattern that repeatedly changes direction at sharp angles.
The border has a zigzag pattern.
spiral: A curve that winds around a center while moving farther away.
Draw a spiral from the center outward.
right-angle: An angle measuring exactly ninety degrees, like the corner of a sheet of paper.
The corner forms a right angle.
acute-angle: An angle measuring more than zero degrees but less than ninety degrees.
The narrow corner forms an acute angle.
obtuse-angle: An angle measuring more than ninety degrees but less than one hundred eighty degrees.
The open door forms an obtuse angle with the wall.
parallel: Describes straight lines in the same plane that never meet.
perpendicular: Describes lines or surfaces that meet at a ninety-degree angle.
The vertical mark is perpendicular to the base.
area: The amount of space inside a flat shape, measured in square units.
Measure the area of the floor before buying tiles.
perimeter: The total distance around the outside boundary of a flat shape.
Measure the perimeter before fitting the border.
volume: The amount of space a solid occupies, measured in cubic units.
The box has a volume of eight cubic meters.
radius: The distance from the center of a circle to its boundary.
The wheel has a radius of thirty centimeters.
diameter: The distance across a circle through its center, from one boundary point to another.
Measure the diameter across the middle of the lid.
circumference: The distance around the boundary of a circle.
Wrap a tape around the wheel to measure its circumference.
diagonal: A line joining two corners of a polygon that are not next to each other.
Draw a diagonal across the rectangle.
symmetry: The property of matching parts after a reflection, rotation, or other transformation.
The folded design has reflection symmetry.
vertex: A point where sides or edges of a geometric shape meet.
Mark the vertex at the top of the shape.
edge: A boundary of a flat shape, or a line where two solid faces meet.
Run your finger along one edge of the box.
repeat: To do, say, or show the same thing again.
Repeat the design across the page.
sequence: An arrangement of items that follow one another in a particular order.
Continue the sequence with the next shape.
pattern: An arrangement of shapes, colors, or objects that follows a recognizable rule.
The fabric has a repeating pattern.
tessellation: An arrangement of flat shapes covering a surface without gaps or overlaps.
The floor tiles form a tessellation.
fractal: A geometric pattern with similar features appearing at increasingly small scales.
The computer displays a detailed fractal.
grid: A network of crossing lines used to divide a surface into regular spaces.
Use the grid to position each icon.
array: An ordered arrangement of objects, often in rows and columns.
Arrange the dots in a rectangular array.
matrix: A rectangular arrangement of numbers or expressions in rows and columns.
Enter the values into the matrix.
mosaic: A picture or design made from small pieces placed together.
The wall has a colorful mosaic.
kaleidoscope: A viewing tube with mirrors that produce changing patterns from colored pieces.
Turn the kaleidoscope to change the design.

one: The number 1, representing a single person, object, or unit.
I need one ticket for the train.
two: The number 2, representing one more than a single unit.
three: The number 3, representing one more than two units.
four: The number 4, representing one more than three units.
There are four chairs around the table.
five: The number 5, representing one more than four units.
We need five plates for dinner.
six: The number 6, representing one more than five units.
seven: The number 7, representing one more than six units.
eight: The number 8, representing one more than seven units.
nine: The number 9, representing one more than eight units.
ten: The number 10, representing one more than nine units.
eleven: The number 11, representing one more than ten units.
Eleven people are waiting for the bus.
twelve: The number 12, representing one more than eleven units.
The baker puts twelve rolls on the tray.
thirteen: The number 13, representing one more than twelve units.
fourteen: The number 14, representing one more than thirteen units.
The display contains fourteen wooden figures.
fifteen: The number 15, representing one more than fourteen units.
I will return in fifteen minutes.

mother: A female parent who raises or cares for a child.
My mother called to ask about my new job.
father: A male parent who raises or cares for a child.
Her father helped her move into the apartment.
siblings: Brothers and sisters in the same family.
My siblings live in different cities.
twin: One of two children born from the same pregnancy.
My twin and I have the same birthday.
mom: An informal word for a female parent.
I called my mom after work.
morning-routine: The usual activities you do after waking up to start your day.
Breakfast is part of my morning routine.
trust: Confidence that someone is honest, reliable, and will treat you well.
Trust grows when family members keep their promises.
protection: The act of keeping someone safe from harm or danger.
The family offered protection during a difficult time.
bond: A close connection between people who care about one another.
They share a strong family bond.
heritage: Traditions, values, and history passed down from earlier generations.
The family celebrates its cultural heritage.
